h: Shabbos Preserves the Holiness of Yisrael Even in Exile

p: בְּסוֹף פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ כְּתִיב (וַיִּקְרָא כו, ב)
At the end of this parshah is written (Vayikra 26:2):
And this verse was said in the same form
And Rashi cites from Toras Kohanim:
"Corresponding to this one sold to a gentile,
Since my master engages in immorality,
I too will be like him;
הוֹאִיל וְרַבִּי עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְכוּלֵּי
since my master worships idols, etc.;
since my master desecrates Shabbos, etc."
And why did it take specifically
which is not mentioned at all in the verse.
that one is sold as a slave
is because of blemishing the bris;
If so, there is reason to worry:
in his being sold as a slave?
on account of blemishing the bris,
and Egypt is "the nakedness of the land"
could they not become further corrupted?
And in truth all the exiles
כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ (דְּבָרִים ח, ה)
"He who spares his rod hates his son, etc."
and fenced herself off from immorality,
and all the women were fenced off in her merit;
and all the males were fenced off in his merit."
And this is why the Toras Kohanim mentions
for this was the main reason
that he was sold as a slave,
not to learn, Heaven forbid, from his master's deeds,
And the Torah taught him counsel for this,
and the six days of work
that is, the counsel for the separation
הוּא עַל יְדֵי ג׳ הַבְדָּלוֹת אֵלּוּ
רַק לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם אֱלִילִים (וַיִּקְרָא כו, א)
"You shall not make idols for yourselves" (Vayikra 26:1);
you shall not make for yourselves,"
you will end up making them gods"
(and so it is in Toras Kohanim there);
"Do not turn to your own understanding"
in the days of the Avos,
is forbidden even for bowing to the Most High,
That is, the yetzer hara can
and to say that he should learn from his master's deeds:
just as his master worships idols,
will do as he does — for the Most High,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים יב, ל)
in the manner of what is said (Devarim 12:30):
and I will do so too."
And about this the Torah warned
to the words of the yetzer hara,
which sits at the openings of the heart
it disguises itself as a guide to the way of Hashem for good
and seeks to make darkness into light;
and this corresponds to the separation
corresponding to the separation between the seventh day
and the six days of work
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
"This is the Shabbos of Shabbos eve,
only it is the keeping that is from man's side.
"and I separated you from the nations
when he is mixed among the nations
And the main thing for this
and keeps his hand from doing any evil"
And through this he can be saved
from learning, Heaven forbid, from his master's deeds,
to sink further into the blemish.
אוֹ דוֹדוֹ אוֹ בֶן דּוֹדוֹ יִגְאָלֶנּוּ
